CheckTitle: Ensure hardware MFA is enabled for the 'root' user account
Description: The root user must be protected with a hardware MFA device (FIDO2/U2F security key or hardware TOTP token). Virtual MFA provides lower assurance than hardware MFA for the most privileged identity in the account, as virtual MFA seeds can be stolen via malware.
Risk: Software-based virtual MFA can be exfiltrated remotely via malware or phishing of the TOTP seed. Hardware MFA requires physical possession of a device and cannot be remotely exfiltrated, providing stronger protection for the highest-privilege account.
Remediation: Register a hardware MFA device (FIDO2 security key or hardware OTP token) for the root account via the AWS Management Console under Security credentials.
SeverityBasis: AWS Security Hub FSBP IAM.6 (ASFF score 90.0 = CRITICAL); CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0 Control 1.6 (Level 1)
AuthoritativeSource: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0; AWS Security Hub FSBP
